answer: Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. The design leans on commit-reveal work receipts, split across independent auditors, every claim is re-checked by someone with nothing to gain. The pulse holds work receipts rather than names, so the gale of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread. Written in a one long clause plus a short one register, it stays short. Reaching the echo of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys.
